s1.syndrome_frame: Acute urinary tract infection with possible obstructive uropathy and concern for malignancy in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: Escherichia coli growth in blood and urine cultures
Nodular thickening of the bladder wall on CT
key_facts: Immunosuppressive therapy with prednisone and tacrolimus
Urinalysis positive for leukocyte esterase, nitrites, and white blood cells
Blood and urine cultures grow Escherichia coli
CT of the abdomen and pelvis shows non-obstructing right nephrolithiasis
CT of the abdomen and pelvis shows irregular, nodular thickening of the bladder wall

shortlist.label: Urinary tract infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has symptoms of fever, flank pain, and foul-smelling urine, with laboratory confirmation of Escherichia coli in blood and urine cultures

shortlist.label: Cystitis
shortlist.why_kept: Urinalysis is positive for leukocyte esterase, nitrites, and white blood cells, and CT scan shows irregular, nodular thickening of the bladder wall

shortlist.label: Pyelonephritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has leukocytosis and hyponatremia, with CT scan showing non-obstructing right nephrolithiasis

shortlist.label: Bladder cancer
shortlist.why_kept: CT scan shows irregular, nodular thickening of the bladder wall, suspicious for neoplasm, in a patient with a history of smoking

shortlist.label: Ureteral obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has non-obstructing right nephrolithiasis, but symptoms and laboratory results suggest possible obstructive uropathy

raw.rationale: The patient presents with fever, flank pain, and foul-smelling urine, and laboratory studies show leukocytosis, positive urinalysis, and blood and urine cultures growing Escherichia coli, all of which are consistent with a urinary tract infection.

rejected.label: Cystitis
rejected.why: While cystitis is a type of urinary tract infection, the patient's symptoms and laboratory results suggest an infection that may involve the upper urinary tract as well.

rejected.label: Pyelonephritis
rejected.why: Although the patient has flank pain and fever, the CT scan shows non-obstructing nephrolithiasis, but does not specifically indicate pyelonephritis.

rejected.label: Bladder cancer
rejected.why: The irregular, nodular thickening of the bladder wall is suspicious for neoplasm, but the patient's acute symptoms and laboratory results are more consistent with an infection.

rejected.label: Ureteral obstruction
rejected.why: The CT scan shows non-obstructing nephrolithiasis, which suggests that there is no obstruction in the ureter.
